statement.excerpt: The answer is simple: there won’t be money for venture capital for a while. Those AI holdings are going to be worth, at best, 50%, if they retain any value at all. Once one of these startups die, a panic will ensue, sending venture capitalists scrambling to get their holdings acquired, until there’s little or no investor interest left.

from_speaker: there won’t be money for venture capital for a while
Once one of these startups die

our_interpretation: Read the passage as a linked forecast of a startup failure followed by broad financing distress and losses in venture-capital AI holdings.
The most direct referents are the seven named startups, with OpenAI and Anthropic also discussed immediately before the forecast.
A qualifying death means business failure or liquidation, not merely acquisition, product retirement or a temporary outage.
Read 50% as half the comparable pre-collapse holding value. The text does not specify peak value, cost basis or a portfolio weighting.
For a while describes persistence, not a calendar deadline.
If they retain any value allows a zero recovery; it is not a separate antecedent.
The first two sentences can also be read as unconditional forecasts. This assessment follows the supplied conditional formulation.
criteria.support_condition: After a qualifying startup failure, comparable holding values fall to at most half their pre-collapse values, while fundraising, acquisition efforts and investment activity establish sustained broad panic and little remaining investor interest.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a qualifying failure and a sufficiently defined observation window, comparable holdings and financing activity clearly fail to show the predicted collapse. Without a specified window, a short period of continued investment is insufficient.
